q1Title: Which paragraph is this sentence from?
q1Expl: This paraphrases the prompt in one sentence — a textbook Introduction.
q2Title: Which paragraph is this sentence from?
q2Expl: A big-picture trend with no numbers, signalled by "Overall" — this is the Overview.
q3Title: Which paragraph is this sentence from?
q3Expl: Specific figures supporting a claim belong in a Body Paragraph, never the Overview.
q4Title: Which paragraph is this sentence from?
q4Expl: A macro-trend with no data — this is the Overview, again signalled by "Overall".
q5Title: Which paragraph is this sentence from?
q5Expl: A one-sentence paraphrase of the prompt — this opens the report, so it's the Introduction.
q6Expl: Streaming has the widest gap: 9 hours (18–30) versus 3 hours (60+), a difference of 6 hours.
q7Expl: Socialising has the smallest gap: 6 hours versus 5 hours — only one hour apart.
q8Expl: 6 hours minus 2 hours = 4 hours more per week for the 60+ group.
q9Expl: 18–30 year-olds streamed 9 hours against 3 hours for the 60+ group — a considerable gap in the younger group's favour.
q10Expl: 4 hours is exactly double 2 hours, so "twice as much" is the precise, accurate phrase.
q11Expl: A jump from 20% to 45% is a huge change — "dramatically" is the only word strong enough.
q12Expl: 31% and 32% are almost the same, so a soft approximator like "roughly" fits — the others all suggest a big difference.
q13Expl: 48% is slightly below 50%, so "just under half" is the accurate phrase.
q14Expl: "Peak" tells us the number went up before falling — "climbed" is the only rising verb here.
q15Expl: "Remained... throughout" signals no real change — "stable" is the only word that means unchanging.
